course.title: Soap Making
course.tagline: Make natural soaps and body bars, from recipes to packaged products.

days.title: Soap Making Basics
days.goal: Know the two ways to make soap: melt and pour, and cold process.
steps: Learn that melt and pour means melting a ready-made soap base.
Learn that cold process means mixing oils with lye (a strong cleaner that turns oil into soap).
Learn that lye is dangerous and needs gloves and goggles.
Set up a clean work area with old clothes on.
days.task: Explain melt and pour and cold process in plain words.
days.challenge: Name the two soap methods without looking.

quiz.q: What are the two ways to make soap?
options: Melt and pour, and cold process
quiz.explain: Melt and pour melts a ready base; cold process mixes oils with lye.

quiz.q: What is lye in soap making?
options: A strong cleaner that turns oil into soap
quiz.explain: Lye reacts with oils to make soap; it is dangerous until it reacts.

quiz.q: Why wear gloves and goggles with lye?
quiz.explain: Lye is caustic and burns skin and eyes on contact.

days.title: Safety: Working with Lye
days.goal: Work safely with lye, the most dangerous part of soap making.
steps: Wear gloves, goggles and long sleeves.
Always add lye to water, never water to lye.
Mix lye in fresh air: the fumes are strong.
Keep vinegar nearby to neutralise (cancel out) splashes on skin.
days.task: Write your own five lye safety rules.
days.challenge: Mix a lye solution safely with full gear on.

quiz.explain: Lye reacts with oils to make soap; it is dangerous until it reacts.

quiz.q: Why wear gloves and goggles with lye?

days.title: Oils and Butters
days.goal: Know the oils that make soap: olive, coconut, shea and palm.
steps: Learn that olive oil makes gentle soap.
Learn that coconut oil makes lots of bubbles.
Learn that shea butter makes soap creamy and soft.
Weigh oils on a scale: soap recipes work by weight, not cups.
days.task: Label four oils with what each does in soap.
days.challenge: Pick oils for a gentle soap and explain why.

days.title: Melt and Pour Soap
days.goal: Make your first soap by melting a soap base.
steps: Cut the soap base into small cubes.
Melt it gently in a jug in the microwave or a double boiler.
Add scent and colour, then stir.
Pour into a mould and leave to set.
days.task: Make one melt and pour soap bar.
days.challenge: Make a melt and pour bar with no bubbles on top.

quiz.q: What do you add first: lye to water, or water to lye?
quiz.explain: Adding water to lye can erupt; always add lye to water.

quiz.q: Why mix lye in fresh air?
options: The fumes are strong and harmful to breathe
quiz.explain: Lye fumes sting the nose and lungs, so mix outside or by an open window.

quiz.q: What neutralises a lye splash on skin?
quiz.explain: Vinegar cancels lye, then rinse with lots of water.

days.title: Moulds and Shapes
days.goal: Pick moulds and make soap in fun shapes.
steps: Learn that silicone moulds release soap easily.
Spray the top with alcohol to pop bubbles.
Use simple shapes first: rectangles and rounds.
Leave soap in the mould until it is fully hard.

days.challenge: Make a soap bar with a smooth top and no bubbles.

days.title: Scents and Colours
days.goal: Add scent and colour to soap safely.
steps: Use fragrance oils made for soap, not perfume.
Add colour with soap-safe mica (a shiny mineral powder) or clay.
Add a little at a time: you can add more, but you cannot take it out.
Write down what you added to each batch.

days.title: Project: Make Your First Cold Process Loaf
days.goal: Make your first cold process soap loaf from oils and lye.

video.title: How To Make Cold Process Soap - Basics Of Soap Making | BrambleBerry.com

steps: Weigh the oils and melt them gently.
Mix the lye solution and let it cool.
Pour the lye into the oils and stir with a stick blender.
Pour into a loaf mould when it reaches trace (thick like custard).
days.task: Finish a cold process soap loaf, set and ready to cut.
days.challenge: Reach trace without the soap setting too fast.

quiz.explain: Coconut oil gives soap big fluffy bubbles.

quiz.q: Why weigh soap ingredients?
options: Soap recipes work by exact weight, not cups
quiz.explain: Soap chemistry needs exact weights; cups are not accurate enough.

days.title: What Is Trace?
days.goal: Know what trace looks like and why it matters.

video.title: How To Make Cold Process Soap - Basics Of Soap Making | BrambleBerry.com

steps: Trace is when the soap mix thickens like custard.
At light trace, a drizzle leaves a faint line on the surface.
Pour at light trace for swirls; at thick trace for layers.
Learn that too much blending makes the soap set too fast.
days.task: Bring a soap mix to light trace and describe it.
days.challenge: Explain trace to a friend in plain words.

quiz.q: Which oil makes soap gentle?
quiz.explain: Olive oil makes a mild gentle soap.

quiz.q: Which oil makes lots of bubbles?

options: Soap recipes work by exact weight, not cups
quiz.explain: Soap chemistry needs exact weights; cups are not accurate enough.

days.title: Cut and Cure Soap
days.goal: Cut a soap loaf into bars and cure them (leave them to harden).

video.title: How To Make Cold Process Soap - Basics Of Soap Making | BrambleBerry.com

steps: Wait 24 to 48 hours before you cut the loaf.
Cut even bars with a soap cutter or a knife.
Cure bars for 4 to 6 weeks on a rack with air around them.
Turn the bars sometimes so they dry evenly.
days.task: Cut a loaf into even bars.
days.challenge: Cut bars that are all the same size.

days.title: Lavender Soap
days.goal: Make a lavender soap with dried buds and scent.
steps: Use lavender fragrance oil made for soap.
Add dried lavender buds on top only, not inside.
Pour at light trace so the buds stay on top.
Cure the bars and label them.
days.task: Make a lavender soap bar that smells lovely.
days.challenge: Make a lavender bar with buds that stay on top.

quiz.q: What is trace in soap making?
options: When the mix thickens like custard
quiz.explain: Trace is the thickening point when oils and lye have mixed enough.

quiz.q: When should you pour soap for swirls?
quiz.explain: Light trace is thin enough to swirl; thick trace is too stiff.

quiz.q: What happens if you blend soap too much?
options: It sets too fast to pour
quiz.explain: Over-blending pushes soap past trace fast and it can set in the pot.

days.title: Test Your Soap
days.goal: Test soap for lather, hardness and skin feel.
steps: Wet the bar and rub it: it should lather well.
Check the bar is hard, not soft or sticky.
Wash your hands and check your skin feels clean, not tight.
Write down the results for each recipe.
days.task: Test three soaps and record lather, hardness and feel.
days.challenge: Tell a good soap from a bad one by testing.

days.title: Fix Soft or Crumbly Soap
days.goal: Fix soap that is too soft or falls apart.
steps: Soft soap often means too much water or not enough cure time.
Crumbly soap often means too much lye or too little oil.
Check your recipe weights: soap works by exact weight.
Rebatch (melt and remake) a failed soap instead of throwing it away.
days.task: Fix a soft soap by curing it longer.
days.challenge: Find the cause of a crumbly soap from the recipe.

quiz.q: How long should cold process soap cure?
quiz.explain: Curing lets water leave and the soap harden for 4 to 6 weeks.

quiz.q: Why turn curing bars sometimes?
options: So they dry evenly on all sides
quiz.explain: Turning lets air reach every side so bars dry evenly.

quiz.q: When can you cut a soap loaf?

video.title: Melt and Pour Soap for Beginners

Spray with alcohol so layers stick together.
Pour the next layer gently so it does not mix.
Repeat for each layer.

days.title: Natural Colourants
days.goal: Colour soap with clays, herbs and spices.
steps: Use pink clay for pink, charcoal for black, turmeric for yellow.
Add a little at a time and stir well.

quiz.q: What is an embed in soap?
options: A small soap shape set inside a bigger soap
quiz.explain: Embeds are small soap shapes placed inside a larger soap for decoration.

quiz.q: Why spray alcohol between soap layers?
quiz.explain: Alcohol helps a new layer bond to the set layer below.

quiz.q: Why pour the next layer gently?
options: So it does not mix with the layer below
quiz.explain: A gentle pour keeps layers separate and clean.

days.title: Essential Oils vs Fragrance Oils
days.goal: Know the difference between essential oils and fragrance oils.
steps: Essential oils come from plants; fragrance oils are made in a lab.
Essential oils fade faster in cold process soap.
Fragrance oils come in more scents and last longer.
Check safe amounts for each oil before you use it.
days.task: Pick the right scent type for a soap and explain why.

Do not over-mix or the colours turn muddy.

quiz.q: What should a soap label list?
quiz.explain: Labels need the name, weight and full ingredients list.

quiz.q: Why list ingredients from most to least?
options: So customers know what is mostly in the soap
quiz.explain: Ingredients are listed in order of amount, most first.

quiz.q: Why wrap soap in paper that breathes?
options: So the soap can keep curing and not sweat
quiz.explain: Soap needs air while curing; sealed plastic makes it sweat.
